description: The bar chart illustrates the accuracy of various experimental conditions, likely related to morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models, across different perturbation categories. The horizontal axis displays the categories with diagonally rotated labels, including an unlabeled first group, "1st layer", "random layers", "random layers +B₂", "random layers +L₂", "random layers +R₂", "random layers +permute", "random", "random +B₂", "random +L₂", "random +R₂", "random +permute", and "unperturbed". The vertical axis represents "Accuracy" on a linear scale that begins at 70 and extends to 95, featuring tick marks and horizontal grid lines at regular intervals of 5. The data is presented using grouped bars, with two bars per category arranged side-by-side; within each pair, the left bar is a lighter shade and the right bar is a darker shade of the same base color, and all bars feature a thin black outline. The bar colors correspond to sets of related categories: the unlabeled first group and "1st layer" are blue (light blue ~80.0–81.9, dark blue ~82.2); the "random layers" variations are green (light green ~79.4–79.7, dark green ~81.4–81.9); the "random" variations are red and represent the shortest bars on the chart (light red ~71.6–72.0, dark red ~73.1–73.5); and the "unperturbed" category is orange, containing the tallest bars (light orange ~90.4, dark orange ~91.8). The categories are not sorted by value but are grouped by condition type. Notably, the first category lacks a text label, and a shaded gray rectangle is positioned below the horizontal axis in its place.
